title: Normalized derived comparison for finite totals of injective diagrams
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be left exact and additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and use ordinary derived categories, localization $Q$, and the K-injective right derived functor $RF$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $\Delta$ have the finite nonempty ordered sets $[n]$ and order-preserving maps as its objects and arrows. For a strict functor $C:\Delta\to\operatorname{Ch}^{\ge0}(\mathcal A)$, put $T(C)^r=\bigoplus_{n+q=r}C_n^q$ and $d_T=\delta+(-1)^n d_C$, where $\delta=\sum_i(-1)^i C(d^i)$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. For every such $J$ there is a natural chain isomorphism $\beta_J:F(T(J))\xrightarrow{\sim}T(FJ)$, characterized in degree $r$ by $\beta_JF(\iota_{n,q})=\iota'_{n,q}$ for $n+q=r$, where $\iota,\iota'$ are the finite-biproduct inclusions. In particular $T(Fg)\beta_J=\beta_{J'}F(T(g))$ for every strict map $g:J\to J'$. Suppose now that $J_n^q$ is injective for all $n,q$, and that $u:K\to J$ is any strict map of nonnegative cosimplicial complexes whose columns are quasi-isomorphisms. Then $T(u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, all terms of $T(J)$ are injective, and $T(J)$ and every $J_n$ are K-injective. Write $\rho_E:RF(QE)\xrightarrow{\sim}QF(E)$ for the inverse derived unit on a bounded-below injective complex $E$. There is an isomorphism of entire derived objects
$$\chi_u=Q(\beta_J)\rho_{T(J)}RF(QT(u)):RF(QT(K))\xrightarrow{\sim}QT(FJ).$$
The column isomorphisms $c_{u_n}=\rho_{J_n}RF(Qu_n):RF(QK_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}QF(J_n)$ commute with every cosimplicial operator. The normalization above uniquely specifies $\chi_u$. If $J_n$ is itself a first-quadrant total with indices $(q,s)$ and commuting original and resolution differentials, with every cosimplicial operator preserving both degrees and commuting with both differentials, the canonical reassociation of totals has only finitely many summands $n+q+s=r$ in degree $r$ and differential $\delta+(-1)^n d_q+(-1)^{n+q}d_s$; the comparison $\beta$ respects this reassociation.

proof.text: For any strict diagram $C$, set $D^{n,q}=C_n^q$. The cosimplicial identity $d^j d^i=d^i d^{j-1}$ for $i<j$ pairs the terms of $\delta^2$ with opposite signs, so $\delta^2=0$. Every coface is a chain map, hence $\delta d_C=d_C\delta$. Thus $D$ is a first-quadrant commuting double complex and its total is exactly $T(C)$ by [def-sp-double-complex-total]. In degree $r\geq0$ its summands have $0\leq n\leq r$ and $q=r-n$; in negative degrees it is zero. A strict map induces the summandwise total map, since it commutes with both differentials.

source.place: Tag 012X, section double complexes, and Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), finite-diagonal convention; explicit cosimplicial specialization.

proof.text: By [def-sp-left-exact-additive], $F$ preserves finite biproducts. For fixed $r$ put $S_r=\{(n,q)\in\mathbf N^2:n+q=r\}$. The maps $F(\iota_{n,q})$ exhibit $F(T(J)^r)$ as the biproduct of the objects $F(J_n^q)$. Its universal property gives a unique isomorphism $\beta_J^r$ to $T(FJ)^r$ with $\beta_J^rF(\iota_{n,q})=\iota_{n,q}'$. Explicitly its inverse is $\gamma^r=\sum_{S_r}F(\iota_{n,q})\pi_{n,q}'$: the relations $\pi_a\iota_b=\delta_{ab}$ and $\sum_a\iota_a\pi_a=1$, preserved by $F$, give $\beta_J^r\gamma^r=1$ and $\gamma^r\beta_J^r=1$. For $r<0$ use the unique map between zero objects.

source.place: Tag 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor), proof equality Tot(F(I)) = F(Tot(I)); finite-biproduct universal-property expansion.

proof.text: Test the chain-map equation on $F(\iota_{n,q})$. Both $d_{T(FJ)}\beta_JF(\iota_{n,q})$ and $\beta_JF(d_{T(J)})F(\iota_{n,q})$ equal $\sum_i(-1)^i\iota_{n+1,q}'F(d^i)+(-1)^n\iota_{n,q+1}'F(d_J)$, because an additive functor preserves sums and negatives. Equality on the finite-biproduct inclusions proves that $\beta_J$ is a chain isomorphism. For a strict map $g:J\to J'$, both $T(Fg)\beta_J$ and $\beta_{J'}F(T(g))$ send $F(\iota_{n,q})$ to the target inclusion composed with $F(g_n^q)$. They therefore agree, proving the asserted naturality. Neither calculation uses injectivity or left exactness.

source.place: Tag 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor), finite-total equality, with the differential and naturality checked on each summand.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] to the bicomplex map induced by $u$. To match its convention that the resolution columns are $(D.\mathrm{flip}).X(n)$, take $D_C^{q,n}=C_n^q$. Each such column map is $u_n$, a quasi-isomorphism by hypothesis. The total in the swapped convention has differential $d_C+(-1)^q\delta$. It is naturally chain-isomorphic to $T(C)$: on $C_n^q$ multiply by $(-1)^{nq}$ and interchange the labels. For $\delta$ the target multiplier is $(-1)^{(n+1)q}=(-1)^q(-1)^{nq}$, and for $d_C$ it satisfies $(-1)^n(-1)^{n(q+1)}=(-1)^{nq}$. This isomorphism commutes with $u$, so the quasi-isomorphism of swapped totals given by the cited node is exactly $T(u)$ up to these chain isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), finite-diagonal column-comparison form carried by the cited node; explicit index transposition and signs.

proof.text: Every term of $T(J)$ is a finite biproduct of injectives, and its injectivity follows directly from [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Indeed, given a mono $m:M\hookrightarrow N$ and $x:M\to T(J)^r$, extend each component $\pi_{n,q}x$ along $m$ using injectivity of $J_n^q$, obtaining $y_{n,q}:N\to J_n^q$. Then $y=\sum_{S_r}\iota_{n,q}y_{n,q}$ satisfies $ym=x$. The zero object in negative degrees has the same extension property with the unique zero map. This proves termwise injectivity without assuming that $F$ preserves injectives.

source.place: Tag 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor), proof remark (3); finite sums of injectives proved directly by the defining extension property.

proof.text: The total and every column are natural-indexed complexes with injective terms. Extension by zero preserves termwise injectivity. Apply the existing Mathlib instance for the extension of a natural-indexed injective complex, which is CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective at bound zero, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. This is precisely the bounded-below K-injective assertion formerly taken from the larger lem-sp-kinjective-computes package.

source.place: Tag 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective); also the cited node clause (2).

proof.text: Use the existing Grothendieck K-injective resolution functor to supply h. The theorem rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutionsUnit_isIso in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] makes its unit invertible on every K-injective complex. Transport this unit through quotientCompQhIso and mapExtendIso to obtain the recorded nonnegative unit. The total quasi-isomorphism from step 4 becomes invertible after extension and localization. Compose its derived image with the inverse total unit and localized beta to obtain chi. This uses no plus-derived functor comparison.

For any cosimplicial operator $\theta:[n]\to[m]$, naturality of the unit [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] reads $RF(QJ(\theta))\eta_{J_n}=\eta_{J_m}QF(J(\theta))$. Inverting its two unit components gives $QF(J(\theta))\rho_{J_n}=\rho_{J_m}RF(QJ(\theta))$. Strictness of $u$ gives $J(\theta)u_n=u_mK(\theta)$. Combining these equations with functoriality yields $QF(J(\theta))c_{u_n}=\rho_{J_m}RF(Q(J(\theta)u_n))=c_{u_m}RF(QK(\theta))$. This treats every coface and codegeneracy, not just the alternating differential.

proof.text: The normalization is the equation $\chi_u\,RF(QT(u))^{-1}\eta_{T(J)}=Q(\beta_J)$. The displayed formula for $\chi_u$ satisfies it by cancellation. Conversely, since the two factors on the left after $\chi_u$ are invertible, that equation forces $\chi_u=Q(\beta_J)\eta_{T(J)}^{-1}RF(QT(u))$. Together with the uniqueness of $\beta_J$ on summand inclusions in step 2, this proves the required uniqueness with no arbitrary choice of a derived isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 070K and 070Y, unit-normalized value comparison; uniqueness by cancellation of the specified isomorphisms.

proof.text: Finally write $J_n^t=\bigoplus_{q+s=t}J_n^{q,s}$, with inner differential $d_q+(-1)^qd_s$. For degree $r$ the nested sum $\bigoplus_{n+t=r}\bigoplus_{q+s=t}J_n^{q,s}$ has the same finite indexing set $\{(n,q,s)\in\mathbf N^3:n+q+s=r\}$ as the other grouping. Match each summand by its identity map; the reverse matching is the inverse. On that summand the differential expands to $\delta+(-1)^nd_q+(-1)^n(-1)^qd_s=\delta+(-1)^nd_q+(-1)^{n+q}d_s$, so the matching is a chain isomorphism by [def-sp-double-complex-total]. The degree-preservation and commutation assumptions ensure that $\delta$ preserves $q,s$. In either grouping, the composite comparison for $F$ sends $F$ of each original triple-summand inclusion to that same triple-summand inclusion after applying $F$. Finite-biproduct uniqueness, using [def-sp-left-exact-additive], makes the two comparison composites equal. This proves reassociation compatibility, including $r=0$ and the empty sums for $r<0$.
